headline: Textile factory workers in southern India are being filmed with head-mounted cameras to train AI robots that could one day do their jobs, and many were not told why.
score_reason: Human story on AI and labour in a large workforce; first-hand reporting, no change from pool score.
importance_line: Factory workers in India are most affected, since they provide training data for machines that may replace them; experts disagree on how soon, and robots are costly to run there.
summary: NPR reports from Karur, southern India, that textile workers are wearing GoPro cameras so developers can train AI robots on their hand movements, and that some are paid for the footage while many others, such as 40-year-old Shobha Kiribakaran, are simply ordered to wear them. Astha Kapoor, co-founder of the Aapti Institute, which studies technology's effect on people, calls it "exploitation of labor", while she and economist Amit Basole differ on how fast robots could replace workers in a country where, she says, humans are cheaper to run than robots.
